summary: The change implements String.prototype.charAt in its file, following the spec steps in order. RequireObjectCoercible runs before ToString, and ToString runs before ToIntegerOrInfinity, so observable conversions happen in spec order. The `?` propagation is preserved on all three abstract operations. The range check (position < 0 or position >= size) returns the empty String, and ±Infinity and NaN are handled through the range check and ToIntegerOrInfinity. The substring path only runs for an integral position in [0, size), so from+1 stays in bounds. No special-casing, no hardcoded values, no swallowed errors. The only other edits are cosmetic: the unused parameter is renamed to `_new_target`, and one blank `//` comment line before the trailing NOTE is dropped. Both are minor and tied to this function. I only see the diff, so I did not verify the return types of ops::to_integer_or_infinity or agent.str_len (UTF-16 length semantics). The gate report (build, clippy, +44 test262 passes, 0 regressions) supports them.
notes_for_next_attempt: No defects found. Optional: restore the blank `//` comment line before the trailing NOTE to keep the stub's layout. Before merging, confirm that agent.str_len counts UTF-16 code units and that ops::to_integer_or_infinity returns an f64-compatible value.
